headlines.article_text: Home Depot (HD) Q3 earnings 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Home Depot named Richard McPhail as its new CEO effective next week. McPhail currently serves as CFO. CEO Ted Decker had been on a temporary medical leave of absence but has since returned, according to Home Depot. The company made the announcement as it posted earnings and revenue that beat expectations. In this article HD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Home Depot store logo sign is seen in Chicago, Illinois, United States, on August 3, 2026. Marcin Golba | Nurphoto | Getty Images Home Depot on Tuesday announced its Chief Financial Officer Richard McPhail will become CEO of the company, replacing Ted Decker, effective next week. Alongside McPhail's appointment, Home Depot said Ann-Marie Campbell, currently senior executive vice president of U.S. stores and operations, will become president and chief operating officer. Jordan Broggi has been chosen as CFO to replace McPhail. Decker, CEO since 2022, had been on temporary medical leave since August. The company said on Tuesday that Decker has returned from leave but is now stepping down from his role. He will continue to serve as chair of the board of directors, the company said. McPhail has been with the company since 2005, holding multiple executive roles. "We're not going to change course," McPhail told CNBC's Becky Quick. He said the company will continue to lean into winning professional shoppers like contractors and using AI tools to encourage sales. McPhail added that while the company faces more challenges now than it did at the start of the year, it is still winning share of the home improvement market. Home Depot has been pressured by a sluggish housing market, higher mortgage rates and a more cautious consumer. Still, the company has previously said it's seen resilience among its pro shoppers who are still shopping for their home improvement projects. The announcement came alongside Home Depot's fiscal third-quarter earnings report, in which the home improvement retailer beat analysts' expectations on the top and bottom lines. The company said comparable sales rose 2.2% during the period, compared with estimates of up 1.8%, according to StreetAccount. Here's how Home Depot performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $3.86 adjusted vs. $3.84 expected Revenue: $43.4 billion vs. $42.80 billion expected The company reported net income of $3.7 billion, or $3.72 per share, compared with $3.6 billion, or $3.62 per share, the year prior. Excluding one-time items, Home Depot reported adjusted earnings per share of $3.86. Revenue rose 4.9% compared to the year-ago period. In the third quarter, the company said online comparable sales grew around 13%, which marked its sixth straight quarter of double-digit positive growth for the metric. For the full year, Home Depot said it expects total sales to rise roughly 4.5% and comparable sales to grow around 1.4%. Tom Brenner | Getty Images U.S. Vice President JD Vance said Monday he will make a decision next year about whether to run for president in 2028. "We'll figure it out sometime next year," he told Fox News host Laura Ingraham in an interview that aired Monday evening. "I'm not an expert in this but my understanding with a presidential campaign is there's a lot of infrastructure that you have to set up, fundraising, all that stuff and so you can't declare a month before the Iowa caucus that you're going to run for president," he said. "So, you know, I haven't made a decision." Vance has yet to openly declare any ambition to succeed President Donald Trump when his current term ends, but speculation that the vice president has his sights set on the White House has been mounting for some time. In the wake of the GOP's crushing defeat in the U.S. midterm election on Nov. 3, anonymous sources involved in campaigns told Reuters Vance was among the high-profile Republicans who had begun early preparations for a 2028 run. "We have to take messages from that, but the message that we have to take is that the American people want prosperity, they want freedom, they want sovereignty within their own country and they want us to do more of the good things that we've done," he said.
